57042560.key_claim: A new regulation affecting the HR screening AI system is a significant change that triggers AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment, with documented results retained.
57042560.key_support: The organization shall perform AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.

79209585.key_claim: Decisions on continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AIMS are a required output (result) of the management review, not an input.
79209585.key_support: The results of the management review shall include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AI management system.

89837081.key_claim: Conformance is met by documenting the AI system impact assessment results (impacts identified, their evaluation and treatment) in a format the organization judges appropriate for its context, since the standard mandates documentation but not a fixed template.
89837081.key_support: The result of the AI system impact assessment shall be documented.
89837081.cannot_anchor_reason: Partially anchored: the documentation requirement is directly supported by 6.1.4 (and A.5.3, 8.4). The further assertions in the key -- that the documented results must capture impacts, evaluations and how they are addressed, and that the format is left to the organization's context -- are not stated in any supplied passage; the absence of a prescribed template is inferred from silence rather than from an affirmative sentence.

03b9ef69.key_claim: Internal audits must also cover conformity with the organisation's own AIMS requirements and whether the AIMS is effectively implemented and maintained, not just ISO/IEC 42001 requirements.
03b9ef69.key_support: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the AI management system: a) conforms to: 1) the organization’s own requirements for its AI management system; 2) the requirements of this document; b) is effectively implemented and maintained.

04495679.key_claim: The internal audit programme must explicitly consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.
04495679.key_support: When establishing the internal audit programme(s), the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.

04816f41.key_claim: The deploying organization should require/ensure the supplier delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system.
04816f41.key_support: The organization should ensure that the supplier of an AI system delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system (see B.6.2.7 and B.8.2).

048b2e4c.key_claim: PDCA in ISO/IEC 42001 is a continual, iterative improvement loop that must be sustained after the AIMS is established, not a one-time project completed at initial deployment or certification.
048b2e4c.key_support: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain, continually improve and document an AI management system, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of this document.
048b2e4c.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: clause 4.4 (and clause 1) establish the ongoing 'maintain and continually improve' obligation that underlies the key, but none of the supplied passages mentions PDCA or the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle by name; the explicit PDCA characterization would sit in the standard's Introduction, which is not among the passages.

064f34ac.key_claim: A third-party (externally originated) document deemed necessary for the AIMS must be identified and brought under documented-information control, covering distribution, access and use (including preventing use of obsolete versions).
064f34ac.key_support: Documented information of external origin determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the AI management system shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

077629d1.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 singles out AI systems that update their own parameters in production because such systems' behaviour can change after deployment, so controls applied only before deployment are not sufficient.
077629d1.cannot_anchor_reason: None of the supplied passages mention continuous/online learning or AI systems that update their own parameters during production, nor do they state that post-deployment behaviour change makes pre-deployment controls insufficient. The nearest passages (A.6.2.6 on ongoing operation and monitoring, C.3.6 on sources of risk across the life cycle) address life-cycle-wide risk and operational monitoring generally, but do not support the key's specific claim about self-updating systems changing behaviour after deployment; treating them as support would be a stretch.

07a2e32c.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001 the organization must produce its own AIMS statement of applicability covering the ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A controls, with inclusions/exclusions justified by the AI-specific risk assessment, rather than relying on the existing ISMS SoA.
07a2e32c.key_support: f) produce a statement of applicability that contains the necessary controls [see b), c) and d)] and provide justification for inclusion and exclusion of controls.
07a2e32c.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 27001 (the ISMS standard and its Annex A / SoA requirement) is not among the supplied passages; the distractors' premise that the ISMS SoA could substitute is judged against a document we do not hold. The supplied passages also do not expressly state that the AIMS SoA must be a physically 'separate' document from an ISMS SoA - they require only that an SoA covering the necessary AI controls, determined against ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A and the AI risk assessment, be produced.

07feee65.key_claim: In a combined ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 audit, a single set of management review minutes may serve as evidence for both standards provided the auditor verifies the content satisfies each standard's clause 9.3 criteria.
07feee65.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 27001 (including its clause 9.3 management review requirements) and ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.3, neither of which is among the supplied passages; also conformity-assessment/audit-evidence rules (ISO/IEC 17021 family).
07feee65.cannot_anchor_reason: The only supplied passages are ISO/IEC 42001 9.2.2 (internal audit programme requirements) and Annex D.2 (permissive guidance that an AI management system can be integrated with ISO/IEC 27001 because both use the high-level structure). Neither states anything about clause 9.3 management review content, nor about whether one record can serve as evidence for two standards subject to the auditor confirming it meets each standard's criteria. D.2 speaks to organizational integration of management systems, not to the sufficiency of shared audit evidence, so using it would be a stretch.

097d1896.key_claim: Annex D of ISO/IEC 42001 is informative: it illustrates how the normative clauses may apply in a healthcare setting but imposes no mandatory requirements of its own.
097d1896.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex D (and the ISO/IEC Directives Part 2 convention distinguishing normative from informative annexes) — not among the supplied passages
097d1896.cannot_anchor_reason: The only supplied passages are ISO/IEC 42001 clause 3.4 (definition of 'management system') and clause 1 (Scope). Neither mentions Annex D, annexes generally, or the normative/informative distinction, so nothing in the held text supports (or contradicts) the key's claim about Annex D's status.

09ae6e83.key_claim: A hospital that acquires an AI diagnostic tool from an external vendor and uses it occupies the AI customer (AI user) role.
09ae6e83.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 22989 — clause 4.1 only lists the role labels and states 'A detailed description of these roles is provided by ISO/IEC 22989'; the defining criterion that an AI customer is the party that acquires an AI system from a provider is not stated in the supplied passage.

09db140e.key_claim: An internal AIMS audit belongs to the 'Check' phase of PDCA because it is a performance evaluation activity that monitors the AI management system against its requirements.
09db140e.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 9.2 (Internal audit) and the PDCA/performance-evaluation material in Clause 9 and the Introduction — none of these are among the supplied passages.
09db140e.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages (Clause 1 Scope, Clause 3.4 definition of 'management system', and Clause 4.4 AI management system) say nothing about internal audits, performance evaluation, or the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle, so none of them supports the assignment of internal audit to the 'Check' phase.

0be22fbf.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for a management system by which an organization governs the responsible development, provision and use of AI, rather than technical or product-level requirements.
0be22fbf.key_support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.

0cbb853c.key_claim: The mapping is flawed because an ISO/IEC 27001 access-control procedure governs who can reach the model/API at runtime, whereas the ISO/IEC 42001 AI data-provenance control requires documentation of the origin and lineage of training data — two different risk objects, so one cannot serve as evidence for the other.
0cbb853c.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A/B control text on data provenance (e.g. A.7 / B.7 data-for-AI-systems controls) and ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A access-control controls — neither control text is among the supplied passages.
0cbb853c.cannot_anchor_reason: The only supplied passage is ISO/IEC 42001 D.2, which is a permissive, informative note that security-related controls (see B.6.1.2) and privacy-related controls (see B.2.3, B.5.4) 'can be integrated' with an organization's ISO/IEC 27001 / ISO/IEC 27701 implementation. It says nothing about data provenance, nothing about access control, and nothing about whether evidence for one control may or may not be reused for a control addressing a different risk object. Anchoring the key to D.2 would require stretching a statement about integrating management systems into a statement about non-substitutability of specific controls.

0ccaffdc.key_claim: The statement of applicability must reflect the organization's current risks and controls, so changes such as newly deployed AI systems that affect control applicability require the SoA to be updated.
0ccaffdc.key_support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.

0e74fc58.key_claim: Conformance authority is the assigned responsibility for ensuring the AIMS conforms to the standard's requirements, which is a function distinct from internal audit as a separate verification activity.
0e74fc58.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
0e74fc58.rests_on_unheld_source: The second half of the key — that internal audit is a separate verification activity — depends on ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.2 (internal audit) and ISO 19011, neither of which is among the supplied passages; the supplied passages anchor only the conformance-authority half.

0f002bf0.key_claim: When a harmful AI output occurs and the investigation is still ongoing, the organization should activate its documented incident communication plan and notify relevant stakeholders rather than waiting for the investigation to conclude.
0f002bf0.key_support: The organization shall determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.

1080ad8f.key_claim: Evidence of effectiveness must show the corrective action was implemented and that its root cause no longer produces the nonconformity, i.e. a review of effectiveness rather than mere completion of steps.
1080ad8f.key_support: d) review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken;

1105cbdc.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 requires the AI policy to be reviewed at planned intervals (or as needed) to keep it suitable, adequate and effective, so a one-time approval is insufficient.
1105cbdc.key_support: Review of the AI policy The AI policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

113fc289.key_claim: Verification against specifications does not complete validation; separate validation activities must be performed to confirm the system is fit for its intended use.
113fc289.key_support: AI system verification and valida- The organization shall define and document verification tion and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.
113fc289.rests_on_unheld_source: The definitional distinction between verification (conformance to specification) and validation (fitness for intended use) comes from the ISO/IEC 42001 terms and definitions clause / ISO/IEC 22989 vocabulary, which is not among the supplied passages; A.6.2.4 only establishes that both verification and validation measures must be defined and documented as named activities.

121f8e71.key_claim: Competence evidence from information security cannot by itself demonstrate the competence needed for AI management; the organisation must determine and assess competence specifically against AI-related criteria.
121f8e71.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

1253931b.key_claim: The organization must still control the externally provided bias-detection process; responsibility for the AI management system remains with the organization regardless of the supplier's own ISO/IEC 42001 certification.
1253931b.key_support: The organization shall ensure that externally provided processes, products or services that are relevant to the AI management system are controlled.

144ef67c.key_claim: The AI policy supplies the framework and high-level commitments, while the separate measurable target ('reduce AI-related bias incidents by 15% within 12 months') is an AI objective derived from and consistent with that policy — the standard treats them as distinct artifacts.
144ef67c.key_support: b) provides a framework for setting AI objectives (see 6.2);

145fa273.key_claim: The infrastructure-based scope may be too narrow, because an AIMS boundary drawn only by where systems are hosted can omit AI the organisation actually uses in its activities.
145fa273.key_support: When determining this scope, the organization shall consider: — the external and internal issues referred to in 4.1; — the requirements referred to in 4.2.

152a64ac.key_claim: An organisation that acquires a third-party AI system must still apply AI life cycle controls across all stages it governs (deployment, operation, retirement), irrespective of who developed the system.
152a64ac.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 controls addressing roles/responsibilities for third-party and supplier relationships (e.g. A.10 'Third-party and customer relationships', A.2 AI policy, and Clause 4 scope/role determination) and ISO/IEC 42001 Annex B/ISO/IEC 42005 guidance on deployer vs. developer roles — none of these are among the supplied passages.
152a64ac.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages are only A.5.2–A.5.5 and A.6.1.2–A.6.2.8, which state life cycle obligations (impact assessment, design, verification, deployment, operation, logging, documentation) in generic terms. None of them addresses acquired or third-party-developed systems, distinguishes developer from deployer roles, or states that controls apply 'regardless of who built the system'. Phrases such as 'throughout its life cycle' (A.5.2) or 'ongoing operation of the AI system' (A.6.2.6) speak to life cycle coverage but do not support the key's distinctive claim about acquisition from a third party, so anchoring to them would stretch the text.

15cb90ee.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A controls form a required reference set that the organisation must address in its Statement of Applicability, justifying any exclusions.
15cb90ee.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.3 (AI risk treatment / Statement of Applicability) and Annex A, which are not among the supplied passages
15cb90ee.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages are only Annex D.1 and D.2, which discuss integration of the AI management system with other management system standards (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO 9001, sector standards). Neither passage mentions the Statement of Applicability, the obligation to address each Annex A control, or justification of exclusions, so no sentence supports the key.

17b183f2.key_claim: The agenda omits two required management review inputs: the status of actions from previous management reviews and changes in external and internal issues relevant to the AIMS.
17b183f2.key_support: The management review shall include: a) the status of actions from previous management reviews; b) changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the AI management system;

17b73169.key_claim: Top management must assign responsibility and authority for two functions: ensuring the AI management system conforms to the standard's requirements, and reporting on AIMS performance to top management.
17b73169.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.

1ac02db3.key_claim: The organization must establish and operate an internal process allowing staff to proactively report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system.
1ac02db3.key_support: Reporting of concerns The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

1ad52afa.key_claim: When a new national AI regulation is enacted after the initial context determination, the organization must review and update its clause 4.1 context determination, because determining relevant external and internal issues (including applicable legal requirements) is a continuing requirement rather than a one-time exercise.
1ad52afa.key_support: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended result(s) of its AI management system.

1b0d5be6.key_claim: A static model's accuracy can degrade because of shifting data, so AI system life cycle obligations (notably monitoring) continue into the operation stage after deployment.
1b0d5be6.key_support: At the minimum, this should include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.

1ce517bd.key_claim: The comparison of selected controls against Annex A serves to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted and to identify whether additional controls beyond Annex A are required.
1ce517bd.key_support: b) determine all controls that are necessary to implement the AI risk treatment options chosen and compare the controls with those in Annex A to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted;

20ad8d94.key_claim: A supplier-provided model card can be treated as potentially sufficient documentation if it is appropriate and adequate to support the organization's own risk assessment and responsible-AI approach, since no fixed document list (training data, weights) is mandated.
20ad8d94.key_support: The organization should ensure that the supplier of an AI system delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system (see B.6.2.7 and B.8.2).

23fdd105.key_claim: Omitting changes in external and internal issues from a management review is incorrect, because ISO/IEC 42001 makes such changes a mandatory input to every management review rather than a one-time establishment activity.
23fdd105.key_support: b) changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the AI management system;

24172f5a.key_claim: A competence gap in AI-specific knowledge on a combined ISO/IEC 27001 + ISO/IEC 42001 audit team must be resolved before or during the audit, for example by adding a technically competent expert.
24172f5a.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 17021-1 (and ISO/IEC 42006 / ISO 19011) — requirements for audit team competence, use of technical experts, and third-party certification audit conduct
24172f5a.cannot_anchor_reason: Neither supplied passage addresses auditor/audit team competence or the use of technical experts. Clause 9.2.2 concerns the organization's own internal audit programme and only requires that auditors be selected and audits conducted 'to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process' — it says nothing about subject-matter competence in AI or about remedying a competence gap during a certification audit. Clause D.2 concerns integration of the AI management system with other management system standards, not audit team composition. The key's requirement therefore derives from external conformity-assessment standards not among the passages.

24177d84.key_claim: In an AIMS internal audit, the audit scope defines the boundaries of the audit (what is included — processes, locations, time period), while the audit criteria are the requirements, policies or procedures against which conformity is assessed.
24177d84.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO 9000 / ISO 19011 (definitions of 'audit scope' and 'audit criteria'); ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 3 terms and definitions
24177d84.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages only require that the organization 'define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit' (9.2.2 a)); they list scope and criteria as distinct items but nowhere define what each term means. The definitional content of the key — scope as the boundaries/extent of the audit and criteria as the set of requirements used as a reference for comparison — comes from the vocabulary standards (ISO 9000/ISO 19011), which are not among the supplied passages. Anchoring the key to 9.2.2 a) would stretch a planning requirement into a definition it does not state.

255323d0.key_claim: Assigning both the AIMS-conformance authority and the AIMS-performance-reporting authority to a single person is permissible, because ISO/IEC 42001 lists them as two distinct assigned authorities without requiring that different individuals hold them.
255323d0.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
255323d0.cannot_anchor_reason: The quoted clause anchors the two authorities as distinct items that must be assigned; the further part of the key (that no separation of holders is required) rests on the absence of any separation or conflict-of-interest requirement in the supplied passages rather than on positive wording.

25b70532.key_claim: Integrated implementation of ISO/IEC 42001 with ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 is facilitated by the shared (harmonised/high-level) structure, but joint certification is not required — separate certifications remain acceptable.
25b70532.key_support: Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization.
25b70532.rests_on_unheld_source: Certification-audit rules (joint vs. separate certification cycles) are governed by ISO/IEC 17021-1 / ISO/IEC 42006, which are not among the supplied passages; the supplied Annex D text addresses integrated implementation only, and states no certification requirement either way.

26d79fe7.key_claim: A valid ISO/IEC 42001 certificate demonstrates only that the organization's AI management system conforms to the standard, providing evidence of responsibility and accountability for its AI systems, not legal compliance.
26d79fe7.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Introduction/Scope (statements on the purpose and benefits of the AIMS, including demonstrating responsible AI), and the certification/accreditation framework documents ISO/IEC 17021-1 and ISO/IEC 42006 (which govern who issues certificates and what certification attests); also the EU AI Act, referenced by the distractors.
26d79fe7.cannot_anchor_reason: The only supplied passages are clause 4.1 (context, roles, internal/external issues) and clause 5.2 (AI policy). Neither mentions certification, certificates, certification bodies, ISO's role, or what a certificate demonstrates, so nothing in the supplied text supports the key's assertion about the meaning of holding a valid ISO/IEC 42001 certificate.

271bf759.key_claim: Adding the missing review step, on its own, is a correction — it controls and corrects the detected nonconformity but does not yet determine or eliminate its cause, which is what a corrective action requires.
271bf759.key_support: a) react to the nonconformity and as applicable: 1) take action to control and correct it;
271bf759.rests_on_unheld_source: The explicit term/definition of "correction" (as distinct from "corrective action") is not defined in the supplied 10.2 text; it comes from the ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 3 terms and definitions (drawn from ISO/IEC harmonized structure / ISO 9000), which is not among the passages. Clause 10.2 supports the distinction structurally: a)1) correcting the nonconformity versus b) evaluating the need to eliminate its cause(s) so it does not recur.

27f32165.key_claim: Comparing measured AI incident response times against the organization's stated objective is a 'Check' phase activity — monitoring/measurement/analysis and evaluation of AIMS performance against its objectives.
27f32165.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 9.1 (Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation) and the Introduction's PDCA description — neither is among the supplied passages
27f32165.cannot_anchor_reason: None of the supplied passages (3.4, 4.4, 1) mention the PDCA cycle, the 'Check' phase, or any requirement to monitor, measure, analyse or evaluate AIMS performance against objectives. Clause 3.4 only defines a management system as elements to establish policies and objectives; clause 4.4 requires establishing/maintaining/improving the AIMS; clause 1 states the scope. Supporting the key would require stretching these into an evaluation requirement they do not state.

288b92d5.key_claim: A single management review record can legitimately serve both ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.3, but an ISMS risk assessment cannot be used in place of the AI-specific risk assessment required by ISO/IEC 42001.
288b92d5.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.2/6.1.4 (AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment) and clause 9.3 (management review), and ISO/IEC 27001 clause 6.1.2/9.3 — none of these are among the supplied passages.
288b92d5.cannot_anchor_reason: The two supplied passages are 9.2.2 (internal audit programme) and D.2 (integration with other management system standards). D.2 only states that integrated use of ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management system is facilitated and beneficial and that security-related controls 'can be integrated'; it says nothing about sharing a management review record under clause 9.3, and nothing that denies substituting an ISMS risk assessment for the AI risk assessment. Clause 9.2.2 concerns only audit programme planning. Neither passage supports either half of the key proposition, so no verbatim anchor exists in the supplied text.

29b73430.key_claim: The correct response to a human-competency gap is to identify and document the human resources and their competences needed for the AI system's life-cycle activities, ensuring they are available.
29b73430.key_support: Human resources As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences utilized for the development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, as well as verification and integration of the AI system.

2a6b35ac.key_claim: The ISMS awareness delivery infrastructure may be reused, but the awareness content itself must be extended to cover AI-specific matters (AI policy, AI impacts, responsible use) that security content does not address.
2a6b35ac.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

2b69401f.key_claim: Meeting minutes that serve as evidence of AIMS activities count as documented information and therefore must be controlled under ISO/IEC 42001, regardless of their informal format.
2b69401f.key_support: Documented information required by the AI management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure: a) it is available and suitable for use, where and when it is needed; b) it is adequately protected (e.g. from loss of confidentiality, improper use or loss of integrity).

2b85823e.key_claim: Omitting changes in interested party needs and expectations from the management review is a gap, because ISO/IEC 42001 lists it as a required management review input.
2b85823e.key_support: c) changes in needs and expectations of interested parties that are relevant to the AI management system;

2d291853.key_claim: Fulfilling Annex A responsible-use requirements means defining responsible-use objectives and establishing documented processes that ensure the AI system is actually used in accordance with its intended use and accompanying documentation.
2d291853.key_support: The organization shall ensure that the AI system is used according to the intended uses of the AI system and its accompanying documentation.

2e37975a.key_claim: When an AI system undergoes a significant change (retraining on a substantially expanded dataset), the organization should repeat the AI risk assessment because such changes can introduce new or altered risks.
2e37975a.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 8.2 (AI risk assessment — performing assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur), which is not among the supplied passages.
2e37975a.cannot_anchor_reason: Neither supplied passage states a trigger for re-performing an AI risk assessment. Clause 6.1.2 b) only requires that the process 'is designed such that repeated AI risk assessments can produce consistent, valid and comparable results' — it presupposes that assessments may be repeated but does not require repetition upon significant change, and 6.1.1 addresses planning and risk criteria, not reassessment triggers. Anchoring the key to 6.1.2 b) would stretch a design-property requirement into a timing/trigger requirement.

31b6119c.key_claim: Contractually transferring liability for a third-party AI model's outputs is a valid action because risk transfer is one of the recognized AI risk treatment options, alongside avoidance, modification and acceptance.
31b6119c.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO 31000 (and ISO/IEC 27005), which is where the enumeration of risk treatment options as avoidance, modification/mitigation, sharing/transfer and retention/acceptance is set out; it is not among the supplied passages.
31b6119c.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages require the organization to 'select appropriate AI risk treatment options' (6.1.3 a)) but nowhere enumerate or name the options, and in particular never mention transfer, avoidance, modification or acceptance. Clause 3.26 and 6.1.3 concern controls, the statement of applicability and the risk treatment plan only. No supplied sentence states that risk transfer is a recognized treatment option, so the key cannot be anchored without stretching 'appropriate AI risk treatment options' beyond what the text says.

332c147a.key_claim: Annex A's controls are a reference set for meeting objectives and addressing risks, so an organization need not implement every listed control.
332c147a.key_support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).

3619a258.key_claim: Awareness under ISO/IEC 42001 is not satisfied by policy recall alone because it must also cover the implications/consequences of not conforming with AI management system requirements.
3619a258.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

362a3bab.key_claim: Annex D of ISO/IEC 42001 identifies ISO/IEC 27001 (information security management) as the management system standard most closely integrated with an AI management system, because AI governance and information security share closely related requirements and risks.
362a3bab.key_support: Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization.

379b53fe.key_claim: Following significant expansion of the AI portfolio, the organization should reassess the adequacy of the full range of AI system resources — human resources/competences, tooling, and system/computing infrastructure — rather than treating the original assessment as sufficient or limiting review to one resource type.
379b53fe.key_support: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization.
379b53fe.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor: A.4.2 (with A.4.3–A.4.6) supports the breadth of resources in scope (human resources, tooling, data, system and computing resources), and A.4's objective requires accounting for resources 'in order to fully understand and address risks and impacts'. However, none of the supplied A.4 passages state an explicit requirement to re-perform or update the resource assessment at intervals or upon change; the only supplied 'review at planned intervals' wording is A.2.4, which applies to the AI policy, not to resources.

388b7724.key_claim: An updated externally-originated regulatory guidance document determined necessary for the AIMS must be identified and brought under documented-information control (including version control so the superseded version is not still used).

3dc72015.key_claim: Beyond generic quality/security controls, the organization must apply AI-specific supplier requirements that are scaled to the type of supplier and the risk posed, covering matters such as bias, transparency, and intended-use documentation.

3ddabce2.key_claim: The existing ISO/IEC 27001 document-control procedure can be reused in form for the AIMS, but must be re-examined to confirm it adequately controls AI-management-system documented information.

3e1dc277.key_claim: The status of actions from previous management reviews is a mandatory management review input under ISO/IEC 42001, so it cannot be omitted on the grounds that those actions are tracked elsewhere.

3e8a2825.key_claim: The AIMS owner should determine what information users need and provide it by whatever delivery method or combination actually gets it to users, since the standard prescribes no specific channel.

3fbd1080.key_claim: For a procurement manager whose work affects AI performance, the organization must determine the competence needed, take action to close any gap, and keep documented evidence.

40820cfe.key_claim: The list of considerations in Annex B, section B.9.3 (fairness, transparency, meaningful human oversight) is illustrative 'should' guidance, so an implementer should select and apply the relevant considerations according to organizational context and risk rather than treating every item as a mandatory control.

423162b7.key_claim: No prior formal integration (or existing certification) is needed for an organisation running both ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 to share a single audit programme and management review cycle, but the audit criteria of each standard must be kept distinct rather than merged into one unified criterion set.

42c1833c.key_claim: A clause 7.3 awareness procedure carried over from ISO/IEC 27001 can keep its structure/form, but its content must be revised so that awareness covers AI-specific subject matter (AI policy, AI management system effectiveness and AI-related risk/responsible AI topics).
42c1833c.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

430a65d2.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001's third-party and customer controls, the AI provider should address the bank as a relevant third party/customer and allocate AI system life cycle responsibilities between itself and the bank.

45f0ede4.key_claim: Before release, a newly drafted documented-information template must be reviewed and approved for suitability and adequacy, by whatever means the organization defines.

470d5d29.key_claim: Awareness of the AI policy must extend to all persons doing work under the organization's control, not just direct employees, and therefore covers contractors and outsourced staff.

4752d3f8.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 additionally requires the AI policy to be available as documented information, communicated within the organization, and available to interested parties as appropriate.

48a7beb0.key_claim: The EU AI Act structures obligations on a phased, risk-tiered basis, with stricter requirements for higher-risk AI systems under a timetable that has already been amended.

48fdee0b.key_claim: Competence records held under the organization's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS (risk assessment, asset management) do not by themselves satisfy ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.2 for AI-specific roles, because clause 7.2 demands competence relevant to AI performance, which is a distinct body of knowledge from information security competence.
48fdee0b.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

4a264b42.key_claim: A single set of management review minutes can serve as evidence for both an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO/IEC 42001 AIMS, but only if the auditor confirms the record actually addresses each standard's clause 9.3 management review inputs.

Anchoring the key to that D.2 sentence would stretch a permissive 'can' statement about integration into a normative rule about evidence sharing.

4a4d28a9.key_claim: The control that most directly addresses undetected post-launch bias is the operation and monitoring control requiring ongoing system and performance monitoring while the AI system is in use.

4b17a768.key_claim: Annex A is a set of reference controls, while the Statement of Applicability documents which controls are necessary/applicable, which are excluded, and the justification for each inclusion or exclusion.

4b696645.key_claim: Assigning someone to audit a control they helped design is not acceptable because it creates a direct interest in the outcome that undermines the impartiality required of auditor selection.

4ba46161.key_claim: The governance gap of no one being accountable for post-deployment monitoring of AI outputs is closed by internal organization controls, which define and allocate AI roles and responsibilities (accountability).
4ba46161.key_support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

4d866548.key_claim: The AI system impact assessment functions as an upstream input, with its documented consequences feeding into the consequence analysis performed in the AI risk assessment.

4ddff75d.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001's communication requirement obliges the organization to determine what it will communicate, when to communicate, with whom to communicate, and how to communicate.
4ddff75d.key_support: The organization shall determine the internal and external communications relevant to the AI management system including: — what it will communicate; — when to communicate; — with whom to communicate; — how to communicate.

4e995733.key_claim: When a supplier-provided AI component behaves in a way that conflicts with the organization's responsible AI approach, the organization should require the supplier to take corrective action and obtain adequate documentation about the component, rather than demanding supplier certification or an on-site audit.

4fa7e0f3.key_claim: Enabling event logs only during the in-use phase can be compliant because ISO/IEC 42001 sets in-use as the minimum, while the organisation must determine which other life cycle phases require record keeping of event logs.
4fa7e0f3.key_support: AI system recording of event logs The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use.

52004aae.key_claim: The gap of having no documented process for staff to raise AI-related concerns is closed by the 'Reporting of concerns' control, which requires the organization to establish a process for reporting concerns about its role with respect to an AI system.

528c0183.key_claim: The organization must allocate AI-specific responsibilities across the AI system life cycle with the downstream partner (covering intended use, oversight, incident communication) as part of AIMS governance, rather than relying on an NDA.

52a41005.key_claim: An organisation may add controls it establishes itself, beyond those in Annex A, to the statement of applicability when risk treatment requires them.

5b0c446a.key_claim: Using licensed/open external data is permitted under ISO/IEC 42001, provided the organization documents acquisition details such as data source characteristics, data rights, and known or potential biases.

5bba26f8.key_claim: Because a 27001 control only partly relates to the corresponding AI management system control, each ISO/IEC 42001 control must still be assessed for its AI-specific intent even where an existing ISO/IEC 27001 control partially addresses the same risk.

5d0d9624.key_claim: Failing to revisit role and authority assignments after significantly expanding AI use is a concern, because those assignments must reflect the organization's current AI scope and needs.

5e9f5723.key_claim: Leaving AI impact assessment without a named owner is a conformity gap because top management must assign responsibility for it to an appropriate role.

5fde13d2.key_claim: Clause 6.1.4 requires the organization to consider the AI system impact assessment results in the risk assessment, making impact a required input to risk assessment.

6049af73.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 certification demonstrates a structured AI governance/management system but does not by itself discharge the legal obligations imposed by the EU AI Act.

Reading these clauses as support for the key would stretch them beyond what they say.

604f24b0.key_claim: Customer controls apply even when no external customer interacts with the system directly, because they cover obligations toward parties affected by the AI system's outputs (e.g. loan applicants), not only direct external users.

65ee65c8.key_claim: An organization that procures a complete AI system from a third-party vendor must still apply AI-specific supplier due diligence, document how the system is integrated, and retain accountability for the system's impacts under its AIMS.

69503a03.key_claim: The organization must provide its internal credit analysts, as users of the AI system, with the necessary information about the system (e.g. how to override it and when human oversight is needed), because user-information controls are not limited to customer-facing systems.

Clause 3.4 refers generically to establishing policies, objectives and processes, and 4.4 requires establishing/implementing/maintaining/continually improving the AIMS, but neither identifies scope, context, risk assessment, objectives and policies as the contents of 'Plan' as distinct from 'Do', 'Check' and 'Act'. Supporting the key would require stretching these passages beyond what they state.

f6672984.key_claim: Clause 6.1.4 requires the organization to consider the AI system impact assessment results as an input to the risk assessment, so results documented afterwards and not used to adjust risk ratings violate that obligation.
f6672984.key_support: The organization shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment (see 6.1.2).

f74447c0.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 obliges the organization to determine, for AIMS-relevant external (and internal) communications, what it will communicate, when, with whom, and how.
f74447c0.key_support: The organization shall determine the internal and external communications relevant to the AI management system including: — what it will communicate; — when to communicate; — with whom to communicate; — how to communicate.

f75f5026.key_claim: The competence requirement is not limited to developers or operators: the organization must determine competence for any person doing work under its control that affects AI performance, which includes a procurement manager selecting AI vendors.
f75f5026.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

f7eb23b7.key_claim: AI subjects are individuals affected by or exposed to an AI system's outputs, whereas AI customers are entities that acquire or use AI products or services.
f7eb23b7.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 22989 (referenced in clause 4.1 NOTE 1 as providing 'a detailed description of these roles'); also ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 3 terms and definitions, which is not among the supplied passages
f7eb23b7.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied clause 4.1 passage only enumerates the roles ('— AI customers, including AI users;' and '— AI subjects, including data subjects and other subjects;') without defining them. It contains no statement that AI subjects are individuals affected by or exposed to an AI system's outputs, nor that AI customers are entities that acquire or use AI products or services; it expressly defers the detailed role descriptions to ISO/IEC 22989, which is not supplied.

fa5276a3.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 sets out the AIMS requirements an organization implements, while conformity is assessed and certified by independent third-party certification bodies operating under accreditation.
fa5276a3.key_support: Certification of AIMS is a third-party conformity assessment activity (as described in ISO/IEC 17000:2020, 4.5), and bodies performing this activity are third-party conformity assessment bodies.
fa5276a3.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 itself is not among the supplied passages; the part of the key asserting that ISO/IEC 42001 'defines AIMS requirements' is only indirectly evidenced by ISO/IEC 42006 clause 1 referring to certification of an AIMS 'according to ISO/IEC 42001'. The accreditation element is likewise supported only by the informative NOTE in ISO/IEC 42006 clause 1.

fa7bfe7d.key_claim: The existing ISO/IEC 27001 document control procedure can be reused in form for the AIMS, but its scope must first be reviewed to ensure it covers the documented information the AI management system requires.
fa7bfe7d.key_support: The organization’s AI management system shall include: a) documented information required by this document; b) documented information determined by the organization as being necessary for the effectiveness of the AI management system.
fa7bfe7d.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: 7.5.1 establishes that the AIMS must encompass AI-specific documented information (so scope must be checked), and D.2 supports integrated use of ISO/IEC 27001 with the AIMS ('their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization'). No supplied passage states in terms that an inherited procedure must be reviewed before adoption; the key is inferred from the combination.

fcb8a516.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42006 sets requirements for the bodies that audit and certify AI management systems, whereas ISO/IEC 42001 sets the AIMS requirements that organizations themselves implement.
fcb8a516.key_support: The requirements contained in this document, when implemented, support the demonstration of competence, consistency and reliability by the bodies performing auditing and certification of an artificial intelligence management system (AIMS) according to ISO/IEC 42001 for organizations that provide, develop or use AI systems.

fce10a55.key_claim: Faced with a competence gap (no AI ethics, legal, or societal expertise on the AIMS team), the organization should first identify that gap and take action — training, hiring, or contracting — to acquire the missing competence.
fce10a55.key_support: — where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken.
fce10a55.rests_on_unheld_source: The explanation's further claim that 'AI expertise diversity explicitly encompasses ethical, legal, social, and domain perspectives' rests on ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A control A.4 / Annex B guidance B.4.6, which is only cross-referenced in the supplied passages, not reproduced.

fd29a029.key_claim: An existing ISO 27001 document control procedure may be integrated/reused for AIMS documented information, as long as it satisfies all of ISO/IEC 42001's documented information control requirements.
fd29a029.key_support: Documented information required by the AI management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure: a) it is available and suitable for use, where and when it is needed; b) it is adequately protected (e.g. from loss of confidentiality, improper use or loss of integrity).
fd29a029.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 27001 (the ISMS requirements the existing procedure was built against are not among the supplied passages)
fd29a029.cannot_anchor_reason: Only the conditional half of the key is anchored: clause 7.5.3 states the control outcomes that must be met for AIMS documented information, whatever procedure is used. The permissive half — that a shared/integrated procedure with another management system is allowed — is not stated in any supplied passage; it follows only from the absence of any requirement in 7.5.1–7.5.3 that AIMS documented information be controlled by a separate, AIMS-only procedure.

fd625faf.key_claim: The management review is a top-management activity conducted at planned intervals to assess the AIMS's continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
fd625faf.key_support: Top management shall review the organization’s AI management system, at planned intervals, to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

fdc45841.key_claim: The authority assigned under ISO/IEC 42001 for performance reporting is the duty to report/communicate AI management system performance to top management.
fdc45841.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.

ffaa8a5f.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001, risk identification and risk evaluation must remain distinct activities because the AI risk assessment process requires separately identifying risks and evaluating them against established risk criteria.
ffaa8a5f.key_support: c) identifies risks that aid or prevent achieving its AI objectives; d) analyses the AI risks to: 1) assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies that would result if the identified risks were to materialize; 2) assess, where applicable, the realistic likelihood of the identified risks; 3) determine the levels of risk; e) evaluates the AI risks to: 1) compare the results of the risk analysis with the risk criteria (see 6.1.1); 2) prioritize the assessed risks for risk treatment.
